newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cemig sees 1997 revs up 7 pct on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Cemig sees 1997 revs up 7 pct on rate hike.

text.p: Brazil's Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig said revenues would rise seven percent in 1997 after a rate restructuring announced earlier this week.

In a statement, the company's financial director Francisco Penna said revenues would climb by 150 million reais ($141.7 million) this year after the government approved a 9.75 percent hike in Cemig's rates.

But Penna said about 50 percent of the increase in revenues, or 75 million reais, would be offset by a six percent rise in the price of electricity it buys from Eletrobras' Itaipu hydroelectric plant.
On Monday, Brazil's Mines and Energy Ministry announced a much-awaited second round of rate restructurings aimed at eliminating cross-subsidies between power generating and distribution companies.
The last rate hike was in November 1995.
